Chapter 6: Faith in Action—Living the Teachings of Christ
You know, faith often starts as this quiet hope—a gentle longing for something better, a belief that things really can change. But the Book of Mormon? It doesn’t let faith just sit in the background. It invites you to do something with it—to make choices that shape your life.
The stories inside are all about real people, people who wrestled with doubt and uncertainty, people who took hesitant steps forward, and discovered that faith grows strongest when you actually put it to the test.
Picture someone you know—maybe even yourself—a young woman, standing at a crossroads, feeling unsure. She’s heard about Christ, maybe felt a spark of inspiration here and there, but still wonders if her small efforts really matter. One day, she tries something simple: she prays. Not with huge expectations, just a sincere hope to know if God’s really listening.
The answer doesn’t show up all at once. Instead, she notices these subtle changes—a little more peace during a tough conversation, a sudden burst of courage to reach out to a friend, a quiet assurance that she’s not alone after all. And over time, these moments start to add up. Her faith becomes something solid, something she can lean on.
The Book of Mormon is packed with stories like this. Take Alma, for example. He started out as an enemy of the church, but ended up as one of its greatest leaders. His journey wasn’t some one-time magical event—it was a series of choices, each one a small step toward Christ.
Alma teaches that faith is like a seed. You have to plant it, nourish it, and take care of it. Most people don’t realize just how patient this process is. There are times when it feels like nothing’s changing, when doubts sneak in, or old habits make a comeback. But when you keep trying, even when it’s hard, that’s when your faith starts to grow deeper and stronger.
Faith, in the Book of Mormon, isn’t just about believing. It’s about trusting God’s promises and being willing to act, even when you aren’t sure what’ll happen next. Sometimes, it’s having the courage to forgive, to serve others, or to stand up for what’s right. Other times, it means letting go of old fears, or just choosing kindness when you’d rather be angry, or hope when everything feels dark.
What’s amazing is that these stories remind us—faith isn’t reserved for the extraordinary. It’s for anyone who’s willing to try, to reach out, to take that next little step. In a world where everyone seems to want certainty and total control, the Book of Mormon points to a different way: a journey where faith is all about moving forward, not reaching some final destination.
And every small act of trust? It brings you just a little closer to Christ.
